**Triage: `documentation` · `priority:p3` · `domain:engine` (`packages/platform-objects`) · type `Task` · `pm:blocked` on #14318.** First grading, `finding` comes off.

**The widening is not owed yet — checked on `origin/main` @ `5c9e40a`:**

- `git grep recordRejectedMessage -- packages/` → **0**
- `git grep "rejected before delivery" -- packages/` → **0**
- `packages/platform-objects/src/audit/sys-email.object.ts:195` → `description: 'Transport error message when status=failed'`

PR objectstack-ai/objectstack#14371 is still **open and in draft**, so the column does not yet carry pre-delivery rejections and the description is accurate today. Editing it now would make the field help describe a behaviour the platform does not have.

**Blocked on the issue, not the PR.** `Blocked-by: #14318` — objectstack-ai/objectstack#14371 says "Fixes #14318", so the issue closes when the PR merges and the unlock sweep fires off a state it actually reads. Pointing the reverse index at a draft PR would leave it dangling if that PR is superseded.

⚠️ **One thing that will bite whoever takes this, found while verifying the face.** The string is in **two** places:

- `packages/platform-objects/src/audit/sys-email.object.ts:195` — the declaration, and the one to edit;
- `packages/platform-objects/src/apps/translations/en.objects.generated.ts:2470` — `help: "Transport error message when status=failed"`, **generated**.

⛔ Do not hand-edit the generated file. Change the declaration and regenerate with the package's own tooling; a hand-edit is reverted by the next regeneration and, worse, passes review because the two files agree at the moment you look. This is also why the one-line change is not quite a one-line diff, and why the filer was right that it belongs in its own PR with its own gate family rather than riding objectstack-ai/objectstack#14371.

**The suggested wording is good and I would keep it** — "Why the message failed — a transport error, or the validation that rejected it before delivery." It stays true under both row shapes and does not name the `rejected before delivery:` prefix, which is the row's own text and could change without this description going stale again.

**Nothing is misleading in the data**, as the filer says: the row prefixes its own reason so an operator is not sent to the SMTP host for a message that never reached one. That is why this is p3 and not higher — the failure mode is a Studio help string that under-describes a column, not an operator misdirected.

Size/model suggestion: XS, `sonnet`, once unblocked — one declaration line plus a regeneration.

**② No merged PR on this card is newer than that conversion comment** — this card carries no PR at all, so the "the card moved on after the condition was written" refusal does not fire.

## ⇒ Verified by content on `origin/main` @ `50d6c92`, ⛔ not by the blocker's closed state

`#14318` closing is only the machine-readable proxy. The condition triage actually wrote is about the tree, so I re-ran **triage's own two controls**, which it recorded as `0` on 2026-09-02:

| control | 2026-09-02 | now @ `50d6c92` |
|:--|:--:|:--|
| `git grep recordRejectedMessage -- packages/` | 0 | **fires** — `plugin-email/src/email-service.ts:677` (call), `:852` (declaration) |
| `git grep "rejected before delivery" -- packages/` | 0 | **fires** — `email-service.ts:875`, plus 3 hits in `sender-address-validation.test.ts` |
| the narrow declaration still shipped | `sys-email.object.ts:195` | **still there**, unchanged |

⇒ The behaviour landed, so the widening is now genuinely owed: `sys_email.error` carries pre-delivery rejections today while its declared description still says only *"Transport error message when status=failed"*. This is a `finding` whose premise has become true, which is exactly the case the unlock scan exists for.

## Carried forward for whoever takes it — ⛔ this is not a one-line diff

Triage's hazard stands and I re-verified it, **with the line number re-derived rather than copied** (it has drifted):

- `packages/platform-objects/src/audit/sys-email.object.ts:195` — the declaration, **the one to edit**;
- `packages/platform-objects/src/apps/translations/en.objects.generated.ts:**2479**` — `help: "Transport error message when status=failed"`, **generated**. ⚠️ Triage recorded this as `:2470`; it has since moved by 9 lines. Locate it by string, ⛔ not by that number.

⛔ Do not hand-edit the generated file. Change the declaration and regenerate with the package's own tooling — a hand-edit is reverted by the next regeneration and, worse, **passes review because the two files agree at the moment you look**.

Triage's suggested wording is kept as-is (it stays true under both row shapes and does not name the row's own `rejected before delivery:` prefix, which could change without this description going stale again), as is its sizing: **XS, `sonnet`**.

Labels this stroke: `pm:blocked` → `pm:queue`, single read-modify-write, nothing else touched. No assignee to clear.

**Do not hand-edit the generated file.** Change the declaration and regenerate with the package's own tooling. This is why the filer was right that a one-line prose change is not a one-line diff, and why it belongs in its own PR with its own gate family.

⚠️ Triage recorded the generated anchor as `:2470`; it is `:2479` today. Locate it by **string**, ⛔ not by either number.

## The wording, already settled by triage — ⛔ not an open question

> "Why the message failed — a transport error, or the validation that rejected it before delivery."

Keep it. It stays true under both row shapes, and it deliberately does **not** name the row's own `rejected before delivery:` prefix, which could change without this description going stale again. If you think it should change, report rather than substitute.

Changeset: judge it yourself and justify it — `packages/platform-objects` ships the description, so this is not comment-only. ⛔ Do not reach for `skip-changeset` without saying why.

## ✅ ACCEPT — PR #15276

Reviewer of record: `domain:engine` PM seat, session `session_01ARYe3yQTQCUFm5qPYNgKaJ`, R17. Verdict taken against **GitHub and the tree**, ⛔ never against the report. Readings at head `71590c470`, 2026-09-04T08:35Z.

| item | reading |
|:--|:--|
| PR shape | `draft: true` · base `main` · body first line **`Fixes #14372`** — re-read after the patch round rewrote the body, ⛔ not carried from the pre-patch read |

| changeset | present, `@objectstack/platform-objects: patch`; `Check Changeset` green; ⛔ no `skip-changeset` label, correctly |

### Spot-checks I ran myself

**1. The content is actually on the branch, both halves.** Declaration at `sys-email.object.ts:195` reads `'Why the message failed — a transport error, or the validation that rejected it before delivery.'`, and the generated `en.objects.generated.ts:2479` `help:` carries the identical string. ⇒ The regeneration really propagated; the hand-edit trap the card warned about did not happen.

**2. The docs-drift advisory is a false positive, and I measured it rather than waving it through.** It named 3 hand-written pages plus the **read-only** `content/docs/releases/v17.mdx`. None of the four restates the old wording:

| page | `Transport error message` | CONTROL `sys_email` |
|:--|:--:|:--:|
| `deployment/environment-variables.mdx` | **0** | ✅ 1 |
| `kernel/runtime-services/sms-service.mdx` | **0** | ✅ 1 |
| `plugins/packages.mdx` | **0** | ✅ 1 |
| `releases/v17.mdx` (read-only) | **0** | ✅ 2 |

Controls all fire, so the zeros are readings. They were listed because they name the `sys_email` **symbol**, not the changed field. ⇒ The release-owned page is genuinely unaffected, so ⛔ no docs-only PR and no issue is owed — which is the point of measuring instead of routing around the ⛔.

**3. `Build Docs` flipped `success` → `skipped` between the two heads.** That is an independent confirmation the file surface really narrowed: it was being pulled in by the inflated surface described below.

### ⛔ A judgment of mine that was corrected — recorded, not quietly dropped

At 08:04 this PR showed **19 files / +1427**, and I wrote on it ([comment 5536814471](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/pull/15276#issuecomment-5536814471)) that its "37 families green" was therefore **measured against an inflated surface and superseded**.

**The dev corrected me, and the correction holds.** The gate derivation ran **before** the history got corrupted, so its command list was already scoped to the true 3-file surface; re-deriving on the repaired branch produced the **same 37-family set** (29 path-matched, 2 change-kind, 6 whole-tree), re-run 37/37 green. ⇒ My suspicion was reasonable on the evidence visible to me — 19 files was what GitHub showed — but it was wrong, and the more precise measurement wins.

**Root cause of the 19 files**, which the dev diagnosed and I could not have: its own `git filter-branch --msg-filter`, run to strip per-commit card trailers, spanned too wide a commit range and **rewrote the merged-in `origin/main` commits under new SHAs**, stalling `merge-base` at the fork point. Content was never affected — only commit-message metadata, and downstream GitHub's diff attribution. Repaired by merging current `origin/main` again (⛔ no rebase, ⛔ no force-push). `merge-base` now resolves to `origin/main`'s tip.

⚠️ **One residue, judged harmless and stated rather than hidden:** the PR's commit list still shows 8 entries, including orphaned duplicate-content commits from the rewrite. A merge-only fix cannot remove them without a rebase/force-push, which I refused and am not relaxing for tidiness. This repo lands via squash (#15220 landed as a single `c393b56f`), so `main` will carry one commit whose content is the 3-file net diff — the orphans do not reach it.

### Deviations

None from the brief. The wording is triage's verbatim, the regeneration used the package's own tooling (`check-i18n-bundles.mjs --write`), and the dev additionally ran `check:i18n-stale-fill` — the gate specifically for a *revised* source string — reporting 0 stale-fill leaves. It also confirmed no other package or bundle carries the old string.

### Landing

Flipping ready and enqueueing. ⛔ Nothing merges outside the queue.
